article.title: The Two Badges, One Address Journal
article.description: Ananya (31, Google ORR) & Siddharth (33, Intel Marathahalli)'s commute-equation search — buying a 3BHK within a measured 800m walk of the Blue Line ORR stations, before the trains arrive and the repricing finishes.
article.quote: "Her standup is at 9:30. His is at 9:00. The flat must solve both."

tabs.title: Who they are
tabs.description: Getting to know Ananya (31, Google ORR Ecospace) & Siddharth Joshi (33, Intel Marathahalli) — a DINK couple whose entire home search is a commute equation: walkable to a Blue Line metro station, both offices under 35 minutes door-to-door, and a guest room for quarterly parent visits.

buyers.name: Ananya Joshi
buyers.description: The measured-walk mapper. She gamified the search into concentric walking-distance rings around station candidates, colored by price per sqft. Non-negotiable: a real balcony facing away from the road — 'I will not pay ₹2 crore to stare at a service lane.'

buyers.name: Siddharth Joshi
buyers.description: The acceleration-noise auditor. Brought a decibel app to site visits and reads metro-adjacent acoustics papers for fun. Spent his 33rd birthday stationary near Ibblur junction for 55 minutes — the moment his commute became a thesis.

tabs.name: Journey

tabs.title: The commute becomes a thesis.
tabs.description: From 4,000 donated hours of ORR traffic to a measured-walk map — and the realisation that buying ahead of the metro's opening was itself a clock they had to beat.

roadmapNodes.title: L1: The Measured-Walk Epiphany
roadmapNodes.desc: Siddharth's 55 stationary minutes near Ibblur junction meets Ananya's concentric walking-rings map — the thesis is born: buy within 800 measured metres of a confirmed station.

roadmapNodes.title: L2: Ring-by-Ring Audits
roadmapNodes.desc: Every shortlisted tower visited at 9 am and 6:30 pm with a decibel app and a stopwatch — the map's concentric rings graded by measured walk and real noise.

roadmapNodes.title: L3 DETOUR: The Neopolis Hoarding
roadmapNodes.desc: Sobha Neopolis' Greek renders and a possession date in 2027 fail the 'trains before keys' thesis — parked with respect from the car window.

roadmapNodes.title: L4: Dream Acres Leads
roadmapNodes.desc: Ready-stock shortlist firms: Sobha Dream Acres (Balagere) leads — measured 800m-class walk, established community, tenant liquidity for the fallback model.

roadmapNodes.title: L5 BOUNCE: Lost to Speed
roadmapNodes.desc: The east-facing unit is sold while they schedule a third noise-test — someone with worse data and better speed pays token after ONE visit. Over-verification priced.
roadmapNodes.loopText: S5 → S3 Bounce (Lost to a Faster Buyer)

roadmapNodes.title: L6: The Parallel-Protocol Close
roadmapNodes.desc: East-facing Dream Acres 3BHK closed at ₹12,750–13,150/sqft; documents and floor-plan orientation run the same afternoon as a single 6:30 pm visit, token that evening — and the rental-fallback model already signed.

realityChecks.title: Marketed vs Measured Walk
realityChecks.description: '5 minutes from metro' in a brochure means 5 minutes by drone. Their measured-walk rule moved two projects out of the shortlist instantly.

realityChecks.title: The Repricing Already Happened
realityChecks.description: The pre-metro discount inside the rings is mostly gone — the market priced the line two years before the trains. Remaining edge is unit selection, not project selection.

realityChecks.title: Over-verification Has a Price
realityChecks.description: The flat lost to a faster buyer taught them that diligence in series costs the exact flats the diligence selects. Parallel or not at all.

realityChecks.title: Two-Badge Concentration Risk
realityChecks.description: Two tech incomes make the EMI easy and the risk real — the rental-fallback model signed before the agreement is what makes a single-commute flat survivable.

realityChecks.title: The Metro-Timeline Bet
realityChecks.description: They're buying the metro before it runs. Their position on a two-year delay was computed as 'annoyed, not financially strained' — which is exactly how a hedge should feel.

tabs.insightTitle: What I noticed while we were searching
tabs.insightDescription: “They're buying the metro before it runs, and they've done the maths twice — once for the upside, once for the timeline risk. Two badges, one address sounds romantic until you price the concentration. Their superpower wasn't the decibel app; it was writing the job-change scenario down and discovering the flat stays a keepable asset at a 3–3.5% rental yield. That's the permission to buy.”

beforeItems.text: '5 minutes from metro' in a brochure is good enough
A lunch-hour site visit reveals the real noise
The launch discount in the rings is still there to buy
One great office commute is enough to anchor a flat

afterItems.text: Measure the 800m on foot with an app — both of them
The 6:30 pm open-window decibel test is the only test
The repricing happened; the edge is unit selection now

differentlyCards.title: Parallelise from day one
differentlyCards.description: Diligence in series cost them one flat; the parallel protocol should have been the default from the first shortlist.

differentlyCards.title: Carry the measuring app always
differentlyCards.description: They wished they'd ranked every project by measured-walk minutes from the very first drive past, not just the finalists.

differentlyCards.title: Book the 6:30 pm slot in advance
differentlyCards.description: Rush-hour visits book out; the project that got away was lost partly to a visit schedule that could have been tighter.

differentlyCards.title: Model the fallback earlier
differentlyCards.description: The rental math was signed in month five — had it been month one, the lost unit's hesitation wouldn't have existed.

differentlyCards.title: Decide the token threshold up front
differentlyCards.description: Knowing the exact token amount and what it buys (a 48-hour hold) would have let them move the same evening with zero doubt.

chatMessages.text: We beat the metro to the station and paid top of band for the privilege. Still the right call, na?
The right call isn't about one rupee; it's about the walk you take every day and the fallback that keeps it yours. Two badges, one address — finally one platform.

tabs.adviceDescription: For DINK couples buying ahead of infrastructure, the edge is not conviction — it's the protocol that makes conviction safe. Measure the walk on foot, time the noise at rush hour, write down the job-change scenario, and verify in parallel. Buy the walk you'll take daily, not the one some render promises.
